methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in AI & Software. Range: $3.2B - $29.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

private.name: Reflection AI

data.narrative:
Alpha School, a Series A AI & Software company founded by MacKenzie Price and Brian Holtz, was valued using peer-median analysis against a universe of nine private and one public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR). The peer set includes Scale AI, Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, and Black Forest Labs—all same-sector, same or adjacent-stage companies—yielding a median valuation of $15.3B across the four-company sample.

Peer-median triangulation was the sole applicable method given available data. The four peers ranged from $3.2B (Black Forest Labs, Series B) to $29.0B (Scale AI, Series B), with Reflection AI (Series A) valued at $25.0B and Physical Intelligence (Series B) at $5.6B. This $3.2B–$29.0B range reflects meaningful dispersion within the frontier-AI sector, attributable to differences in model maturity, capital efficiency, and market positioning. The $15.3B median serves as the point estimate.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $13.0B to $17.6B, centered on $15.3B. Key uncertainties include Alpha School's revenue traction, burn rate, and competitive positioning relative to the peer set—variables not present in the current dataset. The single-method reliance and wide peer valuation dispersion (9x between min and max) introduce material estimation risk. Additional data on revenue, user growth, and capital deployed would sharpen the range.
